The firm works in a variety of styles, designing everything from a glam Chicago penthouse to a modern farmhouse-style home in Hinsdale. But no matter the style, each space is beautifully layered with texture, unique art, and one-of-a-kind elements.

Modernist design influences bring style and warmth to Candace Mary Interiors' work while detail-driven millwork, pops of jewel tone color, and playful deployment of bold tile add contemporary function and everyday joy.

Centered by Design transformed the sunroom of a David Adler–designed property in Illinois for the House Beautiful Whole Home 2023. Claire Staszak incorporated yellow trellises, cheerful prints, and blue-and-white stripes in the spirited space.

Claire Staszak designs spaces with soul, putting a modern, eclectic spin on classic design. The Centered by Design founder and her team are particularly known for crafting timeless, functional kitchens featuring their in-house line of custom cabinetry. Staszak’s love of historic design is evident in her interiors, which feel fresh yet true to their setting, whether it’s a charming 1930s colonial or a regal prewar residence. The firm is skilled at working closely with architects, builders, and landscape designers, making the process simple for its clients. Centered by Design offers everything from full-service interior design to virtual consultations, making its expertise available to homeowners with a wide range of project sizes and budgets.

Designed for a family of avid readers, the leather-clad entry—a nod to leather-bound books—with its gilt ceiling and roaring fire provides a warm welcome home to this East Lake Shore Drive apartment in Chicago by Craig & Company. The leather walls were made by Michele Costello of CSI Designs.

From chic urban penthouses to gracious country homes, Craig & Company brings a sense of elegance to interiors across the country. Led by founder Joan Craig, the firm is based in Chicago, New York, and Sagaponack, and serves discerning clients across the country. Known for character-filled spaces, Craig and her team look at each project holistically, making sure all aspects of the design, including architecture and art, work together harmoniously. Craig & Company frequently collaborates with artists and artisans to add dazzling details, such as gilded ceilings or sculptural lighting, to make the firm’s spaces sing. The versatile firm takes on an array of project types, and recent examples include a private Chicago club, a family compound, and a Hamptons barn.

In a kitchen by Dawn Reeves Design, sculptural lighting brings bold appeal, while varied cabinet finishes create harmony.

Whether designing streamlined, modern spaces or elegant, traditional homes, Dawn Reeves Design knows how to make the small details shine. Based in the Chicago suburbs, the firm works on a wide range of projects, including historic renovations and new builds, and is known for its bespoke touches. Dawn Reeves Design is able to render 3D walkthroughs, which help clients virtually experience the finished space (and feel confident in their choices).

Deborah Lund Interiors designed a Chicago family’s dining room to be the perfect space for elegant dinners, group homework sessions, and a comfortable place to watch the city’s spectacular sunrises.

Art plays a major part in the sophisticated designs of Deborah Lund Interiors. Longtime collector and principal designer Deborah Lund curates an exceptional mix of contemporary art, midcentury pieces, and vintage lighting in her interiors, blending styles and historical influences for a collected look. Curvaceous furnishings upholstered in tactile fabrics and distinctive wall treatments bring comfort and individuality to spaces, and Lund adds elements of whimsy, such as an ombre stair runner or playful lamps. The firm works with clients across the country and has completed projects from Palm Springs to Miami.

A light-filled kitchen designed for gathering, where refined details support everyday living and entertaining.

Family-specific design solutions assure that every home by Drury Design is functional and personalized. The woman-owned, award-winning design-build firm brings traditional interior styles into a new era creates timeless aesthetic appeal.

Layers of texture and pattern come together for a major impact in a dining room by designer Elizabeth Krueger.

Elizabeth Krueger can do everything from light and airy to dark and drama-filled in her captivating spaces. The Chicago designer works with each client to determine the purpose behind their home and translate it into highly personal and meaningful environments. Elizabeth Krueger Design was founded in 2012, and over the past 12 years, the firm has established itself as a go-to for everything from Chicago penthouses and historic Highland Park homes to Michigan farmhouses and Florida retreats. The firm works on projects of all scales, including renovations and new builds, as well as furnishing, organizing, and refreshing projects.

In this custom kitchen, Elizabeth Mollen Interiors had the cabinets finished in Farrow & Ball De Nimes and worked with Porter Teleo to create a custom hand-painted wall covering to match the cabinetry.

Elizabeth Mollen began her career working in the fashion industry in New York and Los Angeles, and in 2012, Mollen shifted to interiors. Mollen and her team bring a sense of fun to their spaces, incorporating vivid wall coverings and textiles, many of which are designed by the firm. Stone Textile Studio works on projects in the Chicago area and across the country, helping clients to infuse personality into their homes. Locals can also shop the firm’s collections of rugs, wallpaper, and textiles, as well as a curated mix of art and vintage pieces, at their Highland Park store, the Vault Creative.

For Emily Sturgess, paying homage to the history and character of a 1930s Long Island home was essential—but being that its owners were a young family, the living room’s sofas and chairs were covered in Perennials performance fabrics to ensure the room can take on anything. Antiques and vintage pieces were mixed in to ground the expansive space and give it gravitas.

Traditional design is updated for modern living in the work of Emily Sturgess. The designer’s eye for beauty and love of historic homes is evident in her timeless spaces, which are enhanced by gracious wall coverings, elegant antiques, and sophisticated (but comfortable!) seating. Her Winnetka firm, Emily Sturgess Design, works with a talented roster of artisans and vendors who share its commitment to creating spaces that clients are proud to show off. Sturgess and her team take on projects nationwide and are currently designing interiors in California, Florida, and New York, in addition to their local projects.

Bespoke cabinetry, finished in a custom color created in partnership with O’Brien Harris Cabinetry, acts as the framework for this striking kitchen by Goesling Group. Champagne marble tops, natural walnut and unlacquered brass accents, dramatic lighting, and a vintage 19th-century fruitwood table round out the space.

Sisters Sarah and Rebecca Goesling bring design and construction know-how to their Park Ridge–based firm, Goesling Group. The multidisciplinary design collective specializes in luxury interior design, CMF design, and trend forecasting, ensuring that each project of theirs is distinctive. Whether crafting a residential interior or designing a brand identity, Goesling Group approaches each design with curiosity and creativity, resulting in projects that are cutting-edge while still being tailored to each client.

Located in Miami’s The Surf Club, a dining room designed by House of Hunt features a statement-making blue dining table by Based Upon, echoing the ocean views outdoors. An Alison Berger Glassworks light fixture hangs above.

After leading her legendary luxury design brand for over 30 years, Holly Hunt founded House of Hunt in 2021, allowing the designer the opportunity to lend her impeccable taste and wealth of knowledge to interior architecture and design projects. The firm’s projects showcase a modern, streamlined sensibility without sacrificing comfort. House of Hunt’s neutral interiors offer a sophisticated backdrop for blue chip art and one of a kind design elements, and the boutique studio’s refined pieces allow high-quality materials to shine. Hunt continues to conceive bespoke furnishings for her projects and collaborations, including a collection of striking stone and metal mantels for Marmi.

House of Mondi enhanced vintage 1920s style with elevated finishes and modern conveniences in a Chicago kitchen. Lacquered eucalyptus cabinetry in a high gloss finish offers richness and warmth, while glass and polished nickel cabinets visually open up the space. Statement quartzite countertops were chosen to highlight an oversized bullnose ledge, a nod to European kitchen designs.

Founded in 2001, House of Mondi prides itself on creating spaces that tell a story, evoke emotions, and improve the lives of its occupants. Design principal Donna Mondi’s signature style blends luxurious details with rich textures and sculptural accents, and the designer makes it a priority to honor each home’s context and history. This attention to detail results in interiors that feel right at home in their setting, whether it’s a penthouse or a rambling estate. The full-service firm specializes in residential interiors and serves clients nationwide from its offices in Chicago and Denver. In addition to her dazzling spaces, Mondi has also lent her expert eye to collections of bespoke furnishings and stone fireplaces.

Metalic accents, including a custom hood, and a subdued palette give a Chicago kitchen by Ilene April Interiors timeless polish.

A home’s existing architecture and her clients’ personal treasures inspire designer Ilene April’s elegant interiors. The designer’s Highland Park–based firm keeps functionality top of mind throughout a project, resulting in spaces that are livable and beautiful. Ilene April Interiors mixes contemporary and traditional elements throughout its designs, making sure the furnishings, fabrics, and fixtures she selects will stand the test of time. April also designs custom furnishings, collaborating with artisans in Chicago, New York, and LA to add one-of-a-kind elements to her projects. The firm works on projects of all sizes and budgets, assisting clients with everything from whole-home designs to color consultations to pick the perfect palette.

In this Lincoln Park row house’s front parlor, Imparfait Design Studio kept it classic—with a modern twist. A traditional tufted sofa from Jayson Home and a vintage glass coffee table are mixed with a Stark ikat rug and midcentury-modern-inspired blue barrel chairs.

Imparfait Design Studio founders Rebekah Zaveloff and Nick Nichols met while working in the restaurant industry, so it’s no surprise that hospitality is at the heart of their interiors. The residential design firm prides itself on devising spaces that people never want to leave, incorporating vintage pieces, plush seating, and eclectic accents that feel collected over time. The firm has offices in Chicago and Lakeside, Michigan, and works extensively in Miami—from Coconut Grove beach houses to polished Gold Coast condos—and throughout the country.  Imparfait Design Studio’s sister firm, KitchenLab, creates home kitchens that are worthy of a Michelin-starred chef (or just a passionate entertainer).

Deep green cabinets and brass hardware add richness and charm to this hardworking butler’s pantry from Interiors by Jen Davidson.

Designer Jen Davidson creates homes that are made to be lived in and enjoyed, brimming with personal touches and heirlooms that reflect the client’s lifestyle and story. The designer’s Glenview-based firm, Interiors by Jen Davidson, is known for its use of natural materials, architectural details, and timeless furnishings in warm, comfortable spaces. Davidson and her team work with clients across the country on full-service interior design projects, renovations, and new builds.

J'Miracle Designs transformed a once bland Chicago dining room into a transitional modern look. The firm made a statement in the space by fully covering the confined space with patterned wall coverings, brass accessories, and multitextured chairs.

Touches of drama set the mood in the effortlessly luxurious spaces created by Jasmine Artis and her firm, J'Miracle Designs. Working in a wide range of styles, from Art Deco–inspired to contemporary, the firm brings out the homeowner’s personality with statement lighting, metallic accents, and comfortable yet elegant furnishings. Artis draws on her corporate background to give clients a transparent and stress-free process, whether they’re collaborating on a single room refresh or a whole home redesign. The firm also works with homeowners to create stylish yet functional rental properties and helps commercial clients devise offices, hotels, and retail spaces that speak for their brand.

What was originally intended to be the dining room in this stately Gold Coast townhome was reimagined as a Parisian-styled salon by James Thomas. A striking navy mohair banquette extends the length of one wall and offers a chic spot for a cocktail or auxiliary dining for small groups. The neutral walls are the perfect backdrop for the client’s impressive contemporary art collection. The Paul Ferrante center pendant provides a sculptural element that balances perfectly with the graphic art pieces.

Founded in 2003 by designers Tom Riker and James Dolenc, James Thomas specializes in “effortless elegance,” infusing their projects with a sense of sophistication and ease. The duo’s impactful spaces blend carefully curated color palettes, a mix of classic and contemporary furnishings, and plenty of pieces with character. They’re not afraid to take big swings with impactful details, such as a latticed wall treatment or faux tortoiseshell ceiling, to add a wow factor. With over 400 projects completed, James Thomas’ team of 16 has the design process down to a science. The firm serves clients in the Chicago area and across the country, from Beverly Hills to Park City to Palm Beach.

In a Jasmin Reese Interiors project in Coeur D'Alene, Idaho, a primary bath features a custom walk-in shower with lilac marble, a brass English tub, and a custom vanity with an antique mirror.

Color and pattern are the stars of Jasmin Reese’s lively spaces. Ceilings pop with eye-catching wallpaper, rooms are furnished with a well-edited selection of unique pieces, and walls are drenched in color and accented with impactful art. The designer isn’t afraid to mix prints or periods, and as a result, her bold spaces feel collected and one of a kind. Reese, who founded her eponymous firm over 10 years ago, brings a playful approach to interior design, as evidenced by the comic book that introduces potential clients to Jasmin Reese Interiors’ process.

A chic primary bedroom by Jenami Designs evokes the feel of a luxurious boutique hotel—elevated, moody, and effortlessly sophisticated.

The client is the driving force and inspiration behind each interior created by Jenami Designs. Led by designer Jennifer Kole, the Chicago-based firm prides itself on both its highly personalized approach and its ability to translate the client’s taste and lifestyle into exciting, comfortable spaces. Mixing a wide range of influences, the firm’s layered interiors bring together vintage and modern furnishings alongside rich hues, architectural details, and eye-catching art.

The warm, well-proportioned, and well-collected interiors of Jodi Morton Design take the homes' architecture and owners as primary sources of inspiration. Designs are eclectic yet functional, with an inspired use of bold color.

In a traditional Lincoln Park Georgian home designed by BBA Architects, JP Interiors brought in a layered mix of antiques and modern pieces to sit in the backdrop of the room's focal point: a carved marble mantle and antique mirror fireplace wall.

Elegance and charm grace each space that Chicago-based JP Interiors creates. For nearly 35 years, the firm has been a go-to for clients seeking classic, comfortable spaces elevated with a curated mix of antiques and bespoke pieces. Specializing in residential renovations and interior decoration, the team, which includes founders Blaine Johnson and Karen Pearson and design director Haley Pearson, has worked on projects in 15 states, from oceanfront retreats in Nantucket to historic family homes in the Windy City.

The great room of this desert home by Kadlec Architecture + Design opens up to the pool and mountains beyond.

Kadlec Architecture + Design was founded by Steve Kadlec in 2004 to convene a tightly knit team of designers with exceptional experience. At 10 people, the studio remains deliberately small so that they can work closely to give each project their full and focused attention. The Kadlec team has worked on “quietly confident and curated spaces” with growing families, empty nesters, young professionals, and established executives, shopkeepers, and developers. While each client relationship is its own, every project is connected by a thoughtful, disciplined, and detailed approach.

In designer Kate Marker’s Barrington, Illinois, home, a space is accented with checkered floors by Francois and Co., wallpaper and paint by The Little Greene Paint Company, and accessories from Kate Marker Home.

Barrington-based Kate Marker Interiors doesn’t just design homes; they create sanctuaries. Natural materials, soft textiles, abundant light, and nods to the great outdoors bring a sense of comfort and easy-going polish, while touches of whimsy add charm to each residence. Whether building homes from the ground up, working on renovations, or designing interior projects, founder Kate Marker and her team are known for expertly curated spaces that feel personal, functional, and welcoming.

Sometimes Kim Scodro’s interiors are soft and subtle, while other times, they’re packed with statements like a giant fabric bow mounted on a dressing room ceiling, a dining room decorated in tree motifs, or a glossy green TV room. Either way, the spaces this Chicago-based firm creates are elegant and refined.

To create elegant home interiors like those of Kristen Ekeland Interiors requires a keen understanding of how the interactions between texture, sunlight, and color can transform a room's design into something magical at every time of day.

In this stunning 1920s residence renovated by designer Lauren Ashley Allan, modernity meets soul, spirit, and character, crafting a space that honors artful living. Throughout, the home combines eclectic elements and luxurious comfort, offering a tactile blend of styles that feel both sophisticated and grounded.

After earning her stripes working with AD100 designers like Nate Berkus and Kelly Wearsler, Lauren Ashley Allan struck out on her own in 2020, launching her eponymous Hinsdale-based firm. Allen has an eye for timeless and luxurious materials, incorporating elements of marble, brass, and wood that will grow even more beautiful with age. The designer and her team juxtapose styles and periods within their elegant interiors, drawing inspiration from history and their clients’ lives. The firm offers full-service interior design to residential and commercial clients around the world, working on everything from historic renovations to boutique hotels to yacht design projects.

Working with Michael Hershenson Architect and Tartan Builders, Lauren Coburn brought a modern, luxurious aesthetic to a new construction project for a young family in River Forest, Illinois.

After earning her stripes at Tigerman McCurry Architects, Chicago-based designer Lauren Coburn founded her eponymous firm in 2004, bringing an expertise in interior architecture to her design practice. The designer and her team tackle renovations, new construction, and decorating projects, bringing out their clients’ unique visions and collaborating closely with architects and builders to ensure that it comes to life. Whether designing a traditional residence or a modern passive house, the firm keeps functionality and elegance at the heart of each design.

Leah Bolger Design brought together soft neutral hues, lovely textures, and touches of black from the vintage Steinway and objects to capture the client’s aesthetic and spirit in this sophisticated living room.

Designer Leah Bolger brings over 25 years of experience to her eponymous Glenview-based luxury interiors firm. Her background as a college instructor of interior architecture and graduate studies is evident in her well-considered spaces, which showcase her deep knowledge of architecture and interiors. Bolger enlivens her traditional interiors with contemporary elements, and functionality is always a focus. The firm’s work encompasses residential and commercial projects in Chicago and beyond, including new construction and renovations. The studio offers a range of services, including interior architecture, in-house kitchen and bath design, and space planning.

Designed for two busy parents who wanted a calming place to unwind, Lindsey Goddard Interiors layered different textures to bring warmth and depth to a Lincoln Park primary bedroom while maintaining a completely neutral palette.

Lindsey Goddard Interiors updates warm, classic stylistic practices with a contemporary perspective, resulting in elegant, beautifully balanced residences. The Chicago-based firm offers a boutique experience with the resources and expertise of a larger studio, thanks to its multidisciplinary team. Lindsey Goddard Interiors works across the United States and abroad, guiding clients and keeping each aspect of the project on track through close collaboration and plenty of creativity.

M + M Interior Design designed this pattern-reading room for the Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas.

Sisters Leslie Martin and Kim Meardon are the Ms behind M + M Interior Design. The Kenilworth-based firm is known for its fresh and functional traditional interiors, bringing in an eclectic mix of vintage and antique pieces, eye-catching patterns, and impactful wall treatments. Whether they’re designing a lakeside retreat or a classic brownstone, Martin and Meardon are able to incorporate show-stopping moments into any setting. M + M Interior Design collaborates with clients across the county and is experienced in everything from historic renovations to new builds. These Chicago interior designers rely on their time-tested and efficient process to make each project run smoothly.

While bold color is certainly a strength for M2 Design Lab, expressive designs in any palette are a given. Each home is conceived as an artistic gesture, rendering spaces as unique as their clients' tastes, needs, and location.

For a client’s summer getaway in Union Pier, Michigan, Mia Rao Design leaned into a water and sky–inspired palette with Dellarobbia sofas and Geiger chairs.

Chicago’s Mia Rao Design puts a modern twist on classic design, working with a given home’s preexisting architecture and the client’s personal style to devise one-of-a-kind interiors. Founder and principal Mia Rao and senior designer Robyn Swanson work on a wide variety of homes with their team. From historic homes to lakeside retreats, they collaborate closely with architects and contractors while guiding homeowners through the entire process.

Nate Berkus Associates conjured a cozy primary bedroom in a Cambridge, Massachusetts, home, incorporating a mix of vintage and bespoke items, including a custom suede headboard and bed, an Angelo Mangiarotti marble console, Jacques Quinet brass table lamps, a Louis Phillipe mirror and a Louis XVI bench.

One of the most influential figures in American design, Nate Berkus continues to innovate and set trends through his elevated, inviting interiors. Led by Berkus and partner Lauren Buxbaum Gordon, Nate Berkus Associates operates from offices in Chicago, New York, and Los Angeles, and works on residential and commercial projects around the world. From penthouses to lakeside retreats, Berkus and Gordon craft homes that feel luxurious and are designed to evolve over the years.

In a River North condo designed by Nicholas Moriarty Interiors, a Robert Motherwell painting takes center stage in the living area, which features a trio of Boffi sofas. In the adjacent dining space, Moriarty placed a Flos pendant light above a vintage table and chairs.

Every homeowner is different, so Nicholas Moriarty Interiors tailors the design process to each client and the way they think. Each project begins with a deep dive into the client’s lifestyle and story through written and verbal questionnaires and “visual listening activities”, resulting in expertly curated and personality-packed interiors. The multi-disciplinary firm focuses on full-scale interior design and renovation projects and offers everything from interior architectural consulting and space planning to art curation and custom furniture and casegood design. Since it was founded in 2008, Nicholas Moriarty Interiors has become known for its artful, deeply considered designs and counts celebrities, Fortune 500 execs, and artists among its clients and fans.

For a project on Chicago's North Shore, North Shore Nest helped their client make her dark home office something special. Designers Melinda Cahill and Suzanne Glavin coated the wood paneling with high-gloss blue paint and brought in layers of blues, pinks, neutrals, and raspberry tones for an overall light and airy feel.

In 2004, Melinda Cahill and Suzanne Glavin teamed up to found North Shore Nest, their Glenview-based residential interior design firm. The design duo and their team specialize in warm, inviting spaces for families and young professionals, imbuing rooms with color, pattern, and a palpable sense of fun. North Shore Nest offers full-service interior design as well as full-day or hour-long consultations. Clients have a dedicated concierge to keep them informed with frequent updates throughout the design process. The firm works on projects in the Chicago area, as well as with clients in Lake Geneva, Wisconsin, and has recently expanded its reach with new construction projects in Arizona and Florida.

There’s no shortage of storage in this River North kitchen, which Outline Interiors designed with the client's love for cooking and entertaining in mind.

Outline Interiors doesn’t just design homes, it also creates moments of joy for their clients and anyone who enters their spaces. Founder Laura Tribbett earned her stripes at several AD100 firms in New York before launching her Windy City firm in 2015. The studio specializes in modern, tailored, and comfortable style, and isn’t afraid to go bold, whether it’s adding plaid wallpaper to an office or installing dramatic black cabinets in a modern kitchen.

Tribbett and her team collaborate with a trusted and talented roster of architects, contractors, and vendors to execute their vision, and the firm carefully manages each stage of the process–even helping clients shop for a home or start a new build.

In a Glen Ellyn home, Park & Oak paired a deep blue paint color with dark wood detailing to create a cozy, moody feel that's both classic and fresh.

Charming details abound in the work of Christina Samatas and Renee Rice, founders of Glen Ellyn–based Park & Oak. The firm specializes in homes that feel personal and timeless, working with clients across the United States on renovations, new builds, and full-home decorating projects. Park & Oak’s beautifully layered interiors feature natural materials, statement lighting, vintage pieces, and subtle patterns. In addition to the design studio, the company showcases its signature style at its shop, Park & Oak Collected, and at its cocktail lounge, The Parlour.

A primarily monochrome living room by Paula Interiors is accented with yellow throw pillows.

Paula Interiors focuses on helping clients create inviting, beautiful, and functional spaces. For the past 12 years, founder Paula Rodriguez has worked on a variety of projects, which include both residential and commercial properties. No matter the size, style, or complexity of design, Rodriguez’s clientele has always been most impressed by the personal experience that Paula Interiors provides. Rodriguez strongly believes that an interior designer should not have a specific style or look that is signature to their company. Instead, she believes in a style-discovery process, in which the client and designer build a vision collaboratively. Her objective with every project is to transform a space into an innovative room that meets the needs of her clients while still producing a wow factor each time they enter their newly designed space.

Rebel House infused the custom white oak kitchen in a Winnetka new build with luxe details, including antique brass accents, an island with reeded end panels, and a walk-in pantry hidden behind a steel-and-glass door.

Creativity and precision come together in the work of Winnetka-based Rebel House. Led by creative director Marli Jones and managing director Michael Kreuser, the firm specializes in new construction, gut renovations, as well as furnishing and boutique hospitality projects, and is known for its ability to carefully manage projects, keeping them on schedule and budget. Exceptional and eye-catching materials are a throughline in the studio’s projects, which range from sophisticated Gold Coast apartments to modern retreats in Utah and Wisconsin. Rebel House has a collaborative process, enhancing their clients’ visions with their own design prowess.

In a co-op apartment in Chicago’s Gold Coat area, Sarah Montgomery Interiors added character to the living room with wood paneling and a stone fireplace surround. A piece by artist hangs above the fireplace and the wood and suede chairs are by Brazilian architect Carlos Motta.

With a background in set design and as a prop master, designer Sarah Montgomery knows how to set a scene. The interior designer blends her experiences in theater and luxury product design in her interiors, which feature lively colors and patterns, worldly influences, artful accents, and striking lighting. Operating out of a stylish Logan Square studio, Sarah Montgomery Interiors specializes in full-service interior design and renovations, transforming historic homes in Chicago and beyond. Montgomery and her team beautifully preserve a home’s past while updating it to work for the way their client lives today.

In a Chicago home renovated by Sasha Adler Design, the island’s brass legs and custom etageres add jewelry-like details to the space. An oak and glass archway frames the passage into the breakfast room.

Sasha Adler brings a wealth of stylish experience to each project, drawing on her time in the fashion industry and the 14 years she worked as design director for Nate Berkus. Adler and her team specialize in historical restorations and new construction in their work around the globe. From artful Chicago apartments to luxe private planes, the designer enhances each space with a harmonious mix of vintage and modern furnishings and one-of-a-kind details. Sasha Adler Design collaborates closely with clients to make sure each project fits with their lifestyles, goals, and budgets.

Interior by Soucie Horner Design Collective

Bespoke design is not just a nice-to-have for this interiors studio, it's an entire mantra. Each project at Soucie Horner Design Collective is considered individually—and holistically—to craft a solution that feels as unique as the clients, the site, and the particular circumstances themselves.

In the dining room of a Chicago condo, Studio Sven found inexpensive textured pendant lights on Etsy and had them painted a bold plum color, which compliments the 70s art and fuschia chairs.

Homes by Chicago-based Studio Sven are not for shrinking violets or minimalists. The bold, outside-the-box interiors crafted by founder Lauren Svenstrup and her team are a feast for the eyes with surprising color palettes, sculptural furnishings, and plenty of unexpected details. Whether working on new construction, renovations, or full-home furnishings projects, Studio Sven creates a collected atmosphere that’s striking yet approachable and made to work with the way a client lives.

Light and bright was the objective for this kitchen, designed by Studio W Interiors.

Based in Hinsdale, a suburb of Chicago, Studio W Interiors is a full-service residential design firm that works on new construction, renovations, and furnishing projects across the US. From concept to completion, the studio works collaboratively with clients and trades to create beautifully designed homes that aim to transcend trends. The defining philosophy that guides the firm is to create a cohesive home that is elevated and inviting with a focus on quality materials. After studying marketing at Loyola University of Chicago and furthering her education in interior design at the School of the Art Institute, Diana Wagenbach began her own namesake company in 2020. Known for her thoughtful design, she works to create spaces that make life feel calm and inspired. She oversees all design projects to ensure they are a reflection of the client while incorporating the firm’s timeless and organic aesthetic.

Floral patterns aplenty in this dining room by Summer Thornton Design, including the Jaipur-influenced Iksel wallpaper, while real flowers add even more drama.

Summer Thornton Design is known for fearlessly bold and colorful interiors. Headquartered in Chicago, the firm works throughout North America, with current projects including the renovation of a Tuxedo Road estate in Atlanta; a Presidio Heights home renovation; a private club in New York City; a Naples, Florida, vacation home addition; a new build in Mexico; and numerous projects in the Chicago area. Founder Summer Thornton firmly believes that each client’s home should be a reflection of their personal style—their soul, passions, and quirks should be found on the walls and in the furniture throughout the home—so no two projects should ever look alike. With over 100,000 followers on Instagram, her inspiring style has been often imitated, but never replicated.

For this entryway, Suzanne Lovell Inc. combined checkerboard tiles and simple details for a classic look.

Suzanne Lovell Inc. (SLI) is a preeminent architecture and interior design firm that also features a boutique fine art advisory. Since 1985, SLI has created award-winning projects for residential clients in Chicago and around the world, including Manhattan, Miami, Naples, Palm Beach, Captiva Island, San Francisco, Hilton Head Island, and the South of France. An experienced team of professionals well-versed in coordinating all aspects of residential projects, the firm creates couture environments through the integration of interior architecture, sophisticated materials, custom furniture, textiles, antiques, and fine art collections that convey each client’s distinct personality.

Beyond solely interior design, Harvard, Illinois-based The Design Coach fills in gaps in the design process for clients, providing management for maintenance and household services, as well as lifestyle support for both everyday tasks and special events.

Third Coast Interiors revived an original structure built by iconic Chicago architect Benjamin Marshall, incorporating a custom rug from Oscar Isberian Rugs and Interior Crafts sofas upholstered in the firm’s own fabrics.

Led by designer Guinevere Johnson, Chicago’s Third Coast Interiors focuses on balancing livability and aesthetics, resulting in homes that feel comfortable and timeless. Architectural details, striking materials, and one-of-a-kind elements take center stage in the firm’s designs, which range from beach retreats in Florida to townhouses on Chicago’s Gold Coast. The firm works on residential and commercial interiors in Chicago and beyond, relying on a streamlined process to ensure projects stay organized.

For the living room of the HGTV Smart Home 2023, Tiffany Brooks Interiors created a rich look with a dramatic green walls, vintage finds, and a mix of luxe textures.

Celeb-favorite designer Tiffany Brooks creates homes that are truly personalized to the client, whether it’s a Chicago family or an NBA player. The AD100 designer, whose design for superstar Jimmy Butler graced AD’s November 2024 cover, transforms spaces with color and pattern, incorporating unique design elements and accents that elevate each room into an experience. Brooks and her team work on projects of all sizes, from single-room designs to whole-home renovations to new construction, and the firm collaborates with clients in the Chicago area and across the country.

The office of Tom Stringer Design Partners was named one of Chicago’s coolest offices by Crain’s Chicago Business, and it’s easy to see why. The studio serves as an ever-evolving backdrop for interesting things and seamlessly blends comfortable furniture with antiques and touches of home. The result is a tailored workspace that appeals to the designers’ own tastes and those of their high-end residential clients.

Designer Tom Stringer doesn’t have a signature style; instead, he and his team approach each project with a spirit of discovery, bringing out the unique qualities of the client and their home. #4979. A Fun Way to Build Relational Skills

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 5, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch

Our relationships are the source of some of our greatest joys and deepest pain. When our relationships are thriving, we tend to thrive, and when they’re strained, we suffer. In fact, many of the most pressing problems, not only in our personal lives but also in the larger world, such as interpersonal abuse, war, racism, climate change, and animal exploitation, are driven by dysfunctional ways of relating: to other people, to animals and the environment, and even to ourselves. So building relational literacy—the understanding of and ability to practice healthy ways of relating—can help transform these problems.

Yet the people who most need to build relational literacy are also probably the least likely to pick up a self-help book or go to therapy. They may, however, happily spend an evening engrossed in a novel or bingeing on Netflix.

What if we could build relational skills through reading or watching enjoyable stories?

Stories, whether written or on-screen, teach us things, from how a courtroom works to what healthy communication looks like. Research suggests that stories also shape our beliefs and attitudes, for better or worse. And because every story features characters, and characters are always relating—to others, and at the very least to themselves—every story is teaching us how to relate. The only question is whether we’re learning skillful or harmful ways of relating.

Consider the all-too-common bar scene in which an affronted man “communicates with his fists” by beating up a stranger who was making eyes at his partner. Or the many revenge movies in which an aggrieved parent (often a father) seeks not only to catch, but to brutalize, the person who kidnapped their child. In contrast, series like This Is Us portray complex relationships and characters who are nuanced and vulnerable, who turn toward rather than against or away from each other, and who repair after a relational breach.

Stories can also help us recognize difficult-to-identify dynamics, such as those that arise with addiction or domestic abuse. We often see more clearly when we look at a situation from the outside, as observers of someone else’s experience. For example, the film When a Man Loves a Woman reveals how alcohol dependence impacts a family system, while the novel and movie It Ends With Us reveal how gaslighting and trauma bonding operate in an abusive relationship.

If you’re building relational skills through such means as reading nonfiction or taking courses, fiction can be a powerful supplement. Stories can bring the principles and tools described in nonfiction to life, showing what they look like and how they can be applied. This is why, after writing seven nonfiction books, several of which are about relationships, I wrote a novel. I wanted readers to be able to see relational concepts in action while also being entertained.

To get more out of novels and shows as tools for relational learning, you can use a list of questions for post-reading or -viewing. You can tailor the list to areas you want to grow in or concepts you’re learning through therapy or nonfiction (for example, attachment styles, relational repair, or the Gottmans’ “four horsemen”), and use it for personal reflection or for discussion with someone you’ve read or watched with.

You can start with questions like the following:

I’ve always believed that a great story leaves the reader or viewer a little better off than they were before. Whether you’re a therapist working with clients or an individual wanting to build your relational skills, consider adding stories to your relational toolkit. Stories not only teach us; they can help us have fun in the process of learning.

Braddock, K., & Dillard, J. P. (2016). Meta-analytic evidence for the persuasive effect of narratives on beliefs, attitudes, intentions, and behaviors. Communication Monographs, 83(4), 446-467.

Hermann, E., Morgan, M., & Shanahan, J. (2021). Television, continuity, and change: A meta-analysis of five decades of cultivation research. Journal of Communication, 71(4), 515-544.

Joy, M. (2025). A half-hearted death wish. Two Steps Forward Press.

#4978. Korean police book 80 Tesla drivers over illegal FSD unlock devices

Seoul police have booked 80 people for using aftermarket devices to switch on Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” in cars that aren’t allowed to run it in South Korea. Officers also seized 21 of the devices.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case on Tuesday. It’s the largest enforcement action yet against the FSD “jailbreak” hardware that has spread through China, Europe, and Korea over the past year.

Police say the suspects either imported the unlock modules from Europe and China or made their own. One plugged a European-made unit into his own Tesla. Another, an IT worker, built his device with information he found on GitHub.

Suspects also swapped advice online on how to unlock FSD and how to stop the car from keeping any record that it had been activated.

They’re charged under Korea’s Motor Vehicle Management Act, which bans unauthorized software changes that can affect a vehicle’s safety. The penalty is up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won (about $15,000).

The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport asked police to look into it back in April after finding signs of unauthorized activation. A police official told Korea JoongAng Daily that “safety risks were confirmed,” including the possibility of FSD misreading driving conditions. The investigation is ongoing, with police consulting the ministry and the Korea Transportation Safety Authority on the technical side.

Tesla launched FSD (Supervised) in South Korea in late 2025, but only on US-built vehicles: Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck. Those cars are exempt from Korean safety certification under the Korea-US free trade agreement. The Model 3 and Model Y, which Tesla ships to Korea from Giga Shanghai, haven’t cleared Korea’s safety standards for the feature.

And those two models are the bulk of the fleet. Citing Carisyou Data Lab, Korea JoongAng Daily reports that 47,458 of the 229,311 Teslas on Korean roads as of August, or 20.7%, can legally use FSD.

That number doesn’t match the government’s own count from a few months earlier. In May, data released by lawmaker Park Yong-gap showed just 4,292 of 180,684 registered Teslas (2.4%) were eligible: 2,708 Model X, 1,193 Model S, and 391 Cybertruck. Either way, the vast majority of Korean Tesla owners can’t legally use FSD, and some of them paid over $6,000 for it anyway.

The hardware is the same, which is why the hack works. The modules plug into the car’s CAN bus and get around the regional software lock.

Tesla has been fighting the devices itself. In April, it started remotely detecting them and stripping FSD from affected cars, warned owners they’d be fully liable for any crash and could lose warranty coverage, and permanently banned some Chinese owners from FSD.

Tesla & Starlink: The reality as reported in 2021: every one of our Tesla autos are connected 24/7/365 to the company. It was that year that a programming glitch came where some vehicles would not function. That was quickly corrected. In the news today where proof that when Elon shut down Starlink to Ukraine, russian missiles came and killed 5 people, including one baby. ... here is the reality you and me must face: Musk holds the power right now, that if he decides he does not like 'some owners' of Teslas, he can SHUT DOWN instantly those vehicles from moving. It is not enough that potentially, every conversation and communication device used inside those vehicles 'can' be recorded but, as he has proven perfectly willing to do to Ukraine families, so he could at any moment 'shut down' some specific users of Tesla vehicles at-will. this is not hype, fantasy or gusswork. This is how the online active update software communications system works on every car we buy from Tesla. My company is looking into other providers of Sat-Com services, and we are re-evaluating our own vehicle choices.

It’s easy to see why people do this. Picture a Korean owner of a Shanghai-built Model Y who paid for FSD, watching the Model X next door run the same software on the same computer. That’s frustrating.

Tesla sold FSD to owners of cars it had no regulatory path to enable in Korea, the same way it sold “Full Self-Driving” in Europe for years while approval kept slipping. It only dropped the name there this month after Germany pushed back. Sell a feature people can’t legally use and you create the market for the jailbreak.

Korea has now shown it will actually prosecute. So will Tesla refund the Korean owners who bought a feature their cars may never be allowed to run?

#4977. This 322-Square-Foot Apartment Gives Classic Style a Contemporary Update

Some gifts are best kept a surprise until the moment they’re handed over to their recipient. That was the case with this small 322-square-foot apartment located in the Vidny Gorod residential complex, about four miles from Moscow, which the owner, Lara, received as a gift from her daughter, Marta, and her son-in-law. “The couple personally oversaw the renovation, keeping the project a secret until the very end,” says interior designer Polina Chumakova, founder of Lagolga Buro, who oversaw the design. “Lara knew nothing about it and didn’t see the space that they were going to give her until it was completed and she first set foot in her new home.”

In the living room, the custom cabinet by Avantiz complements a vintage table and chairs by Tok. On the tabletop, an arrangement of vintage vases by Mak.buro adds a decorative touch.

Lara’s passion for cooking and baking guided some of the design choices, as her daughter envisioned turning the 322-square-foot apartment into a home capable of welcoming the entire family. “It was important to create a comfortable space not only for cooking but also for spending time together, so that on weekends the apartment could be filled with the aroma of homemade desserts,” explains Chumakova. “Lara has two children—Marta and her brother—and two grandchildren, ages 13 and 9. The family often gets together on weekends and at the holidays.”

The apartment’s contemporary-meets-classic design reflects Vidny Gorod’s architecture and its urban context. “The style was carefully defined, choosing solutions suited to both the home’s size and the budget for this project,” says Chumakova. “We invested in high-quality finishes and carefully selected furniture, lighting, and accessories. The idea was to combine a contemporary, understated design with natural walnut accents and a few vintage details. The result is an interior with a classic character, yet without references to any specific era.”

The wall of the living space is painted an olive green by Little Greene that adds depth and warmth. The Synergy Grace sofa bed by Ormatec is paired with the Firmo bedside cabinet by AM.PM; a vintage wall sconce on the left and an Umbrella floor lamp by Artefact on the right complete the scene. On the wall hangs a work by Ksusha Dmitrieva.

There were certainly some challenges. The original floor plan had issues that required a careful reorganization of the space. “The builder had left a rather bulky load-bearing pillar, as well as two separate small bathrooms. It wasn’t possible to move the column, so we decided to integrate it into the layout, concealing it inside a large closet in the entryway,” explains Chumakova. “This allowed us to create a more functional space while making the structure less noticeable. We also combined the two bathrooms. This created a more comfortable home and also provided additional storage.”

The kitchen was custom-designed by Avantiz and includes elegant vintage pendants.

Another challenge was the lack of natural light. “The apartment receives little direct sunlight, so we paid close attention to the choice of colors and finishes,” says Chumakova. “For example, the light, milk-colored porcelain tile, initially selected for the floor, appeared much more beige in the space than we had expected. We replaced it and also adjusted the other colors to account for this effect, striving to keep the interior as bright and warm as possible.” The lighting design also took into consideration the various needs of daily life, without relying on single light sources. “We planned several different lighting scenarios: integrated ceiling lighting, pendant lamps, accent lights for display cases, and other spotlights,” explains Chumakova. “Throughout the apartment, there are about five different types of lighting.”

To make the best use of space, the design focuses on versatile furniture and solutions that serve multiple purposes, helping to avoid clutter in the rooms. “Instead of the classic light fixture above the dining table, we chose a solution that would maintain the open feeling of the space and not limit the table to a specific position,” says Chumakova. “We also opted for a sofa bed instead of a traditional bed. This allowed us to keep more open space and make the room more versatile: During the day, it can be used as a place to relax and spend time with the family.”

In the kitchen, as in the entryway, the floor is covered with white tiles with black square accents, a graphic detail that picks up the colors of the vintage lighting fixtures.

The layout, however, prioritizes the kitchen, designed to be the heart of this home. “We deliberately wanted to dedicate a significant portion of the apartment to it, because it’s one of the most important areas of the home for its owner,” says Chumakova. “The work area is located near the window overlooking a courtyard: It’s a pleasant spot to spend time cooking or simply looking at the scene outside.”

All the storage systems were custom-designed to blend seamlessly with the interiors. “We wanted the cabinets to be almost invisible,” says Chumakova. “There are two large storage units in the apartment: one in the entryway and one in the living room.”

In the living room, custom cabinets by Avantiz are embellished with retro details. The Dovlet House rug, the vintage table, and the chairs combine contemporary pieces with retro charm.

The color choices help define the different areas without visually fragmenting the space. “We used color to distinguish the entryway from the living room, while the ceiling and the doors of the built-in closet in the entryway were painted the same shade,” Chumakova explains. A natural color palette and materials with distinct textures were chosen to create a warm and inviting atmosphere. “The main colors are olive green in the entryway and a milky white in the sofa bed area,” says Chumakova. “More intense touches of orange appear only in certain details, such as the pouf’s upholstery and the floor lamp. Everything complements the natural walnut, one of the key materials in the interior.”

The entryway features walls painted in an olive green from Little Greene paint and a white tile floor dotted with small black accents. A vintage pendant, and the orange Justyna pouf from La Redoute that adds a vibrant pop of color, complete the look.

In the entryway, the floor is covered with white tiles dotted with small black accents, in keeping with the contemporary classic style. The moldings, found in the entryway and on the wall behind the sofa, add rhythm and depth to the surfaces, giving a modern twist to a traditional detail.

The small size of the apartment required some very careful choices when it came to furnishings. “It was important to find furniture on the right scale: pieces that wouldn’t overwhelm the small apartment and that, at the same time, would be consistent with the contemporary classic aesthetic,” says the interior designer. “So we reinterpreted some traditional elements, from walnut moldings to vintage lamps with distinctive shapes, adapting them to a modern residential complex and the compact dimensions of the apartment.”

In the bath, the wooden cabinet is custom-made by Avantiz; the Evana fixtures by Villeroy & Boch and the Oxford faucet by Migliore complement the vintage sconces.

The finished apartment won over Marta, who oversaw every aspect of the renovation along with her husband. “It was a perfectly successful experiment,” the designer says. “Perhaps, if it had been a more conventional project with the future owner, it would have involved them in every phase and it would have been more challenging. It’s possible that some of the bolder solutions might not have been approved.” In this case, the fact that Marta wanted to surprise her mother also provided greater design freedom, resulting in a space that would be perfectly suited to its future resident.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

The right oil fixes everything, like itch, frizz, and dryness. These are the ones worth your time.

THERE ARE PLENTY of reasons to grow a beard—extra protection from the sun and cold, having something to caress when thinking, or, in my case, faking a sharper jawline. But for most guys, the biggest motivator is convenience. A beard may be easier than daily shaving, but it still needs attention. You have to learn how to trim it, shape it, and use the right beard products to keep it looking good. And no product pulls more weight than a quality beard oil.

Facial hair is naturally coarser and drier, and without proper care, it can feel itchy, scraggly, and uncomfortable. That’s where beard oil comes in. It acts like a conditioner tailored for your face, softening the hair while keeping the skin underneath hydrated and healthy. Dudes with big, full beards may struggle to work a thick balm through all that hair, making a lightweight oil the easier, more effective option.

But beard oils aren’t just for lumberjack-level growth. They help moisturize, reduce itch, and protect any style, from stubble to a full mane. The short version: When your skin and hair stay hydrated, everything looks and feels better.

This beard oil offers the most wide-ranging benefits of any I’ve tested. It hydrates, softens, soothes, exfoliates, and even keeps my beard smelling clean, which is exactly why we gave it a Men’s Health Smell Fresh Award last year. The lightweight blend of argan, rice bran, and apple seed oils smooths out scruff while keeping the skin underneath hydrated, and the papaya and lavender oils gently buff away flakes and calm irritation without leaving any greasy shine behind.

The rosemary-powered deodorizing complex is also a game-changer, neutralizing odor so my mustache and beard stay fresh from morning to night. And because it works on everything—from stubble to a full, dense beard—it’s one of the most versatile grooming products I’ve added to my routine. Clean, subtle in scent, and ridiculously effective, it’s the definition of a multitasker. The beard oil version of a walking desk.

What grabbed me right away about this beard oil is how much hydration you get from such a clean, simple formula. It’s packed with the heavy hitters—jojoba, argan, avocado, grapeseed—basically a greatest-hits lineup for soft, healthy whiskers. Even though it’s marketed toward guys with thick, rough beards, I found it surprisingly lightweight and easy to use on shorter growth, too.

Because the oil absorbs so well, I only need a drop or two to keep longer or bushier beards smooth for hours. And if you’re prone to breakouts, relax: the formula is non-comedogenic, so it won’t clog your pores or leave your skin angry. It’s also a no-brainer for anyone who avoids fragrance.

While this stuff isn’t completely unscented, the fragrance is as minimal as it gets. I have sensitive skin and saw no irritation, as well as no cologne cloud living under my nose all day. If you prefer your beard oil to work without announcing itself, this one’s ideal.

This beard oil has the richest texture of all I’ve tried, thanks to its avocado-oil base. Long beards burn through moisture quickly, and this formula actually keeps up, sinking in deep to soften and smooth without leaving a heavy, greasy layer behind. Squalane—one of my favorite skincare ingredients—lightens the blend just enough so my beard feels conditioned and controlled instead of weighed down.

You also get the skin benefits of vitamin E, which helps calm irritation under the beard and keeps everything feeling comfortable throughout the day. The scent is low-key but luxe: a mix of cedarwood, jasmine, and sandalwood that feels warm and spa-like before disappearing into the background. And despite the small bottle, a few drops are all you need, even if your beard’s edging into Gandalf territory.

I know I said never to buy a beard oil for the scent, but this option is an exception. With a rich palo santo fragrance that also blends in bright cardamom and dry papyrus, this beard oil makes my beard smell clean, smooth, and surprisingly refined. It keeps that freshness going all day, no matter how long my beard gets.

The formula does serious work too: on shorter growth, it calms irritation and helps keep ingrowns from flaring up, and on longer beards, it replaces the moisture facial hair naturally loses, softening dry ends and hydrating the skin underneath. A few drops give me a conditioned, healthy-looking beard that smells incredible without ever overpowering my face.

Hair oil is the most underrated styling product for men, as it hydrates and shields strands to create a smoother base that helps other products apply better and work more effectively. I’ve also found that it’s the easiest to forget. When I’ve recently put my brain cells through the wringer and face a subsequent rise in forgetfulness, a dual-purpose beard and hair oil is my savior—and none are better than Aesop’s

No matter how out of it I may be, I always remember to apply my beard oil (my face is way too itchy without it), so the bottle serves as a nice reminder to run my hands through my head as well. I have a slew of skin and scalp issues, but one area in grooming I’ve never struggled with is growing hair (he said, knocking profusely on wood). Still, when I’m in the early stages of growing a beard, it’s nice to have a boost. That’s where Asna’s aptly named Beard Boost Oil comes in. It’s loaded with vitamins A, C, E, and B to support healthier and stronger strands, while squalane deeply hydrates and smooths the hair shaft. Together, they reduce dryness and frizz so your beard appears denser, softer, and fuller.

To be clear, it won’t necessarily help your beard grow, but it will help it appear thicker, which is the next best thing. However, once you do, it’s a positive because you only need to use a couple of drops to cover your beard.

All but one beard oil on this list comes in one-ounce bottles (Aesop is 0.8 ounces), which makes it even more impressive that Horace’s lasts noticeably longer. The dropper dispenses tiny amounts at a time, preventing overuse, and the lightweight formula spreads easily—I only need two to three drops, depending on my beard length.

It’s also the best pick for guys who prefer a fresher scent. While most beard oils lean woody or earthy, Horace stands out with a subtle lemon-and-mint blend that won’t clash with amber or wood-forward colognes but still feels like a clean break from the usual.

If you’re anything like me, you drink roughly two pots of coffee a day. Just the smell of it gives me a burst of energy, which is what I love about this beard oil’s caffeinated scent. After a rough night or ahead of a busy day when I’ll need as much energy as I can get, getting whiffs of this beard oil gives me an added boost—or at least helps remind me to have another cup.

I also have a love of brown liquor that was likely preordained by my Irish heritage, so the hint of whisky scent in this oil is welcomed, though the smell of coffee is stronger. This is probably a good thing; I don’t need a reminder to have another one of those. Performance-wise, Viking Revolution is as effective as you can find under $10.

Its 100 percent argan and jojoba oils blend keeps whiskers feeling soft for hours. That being said, I do find I need to use a little bit more of this stuff to cover my entire beard than other options on this list. But for the price point and scent, it’s well worth it.

What really makes or breaks a beard oil is the blend of oils inside. You want ingredients that actually penetrate the hair and nourish the skin—not heavy oils that sit on top and leave your beard feeling slick and suffocated. Look for lightweight, fast-absorbing oils like jojoba, argan, grapeseed, avocado, and castor, which sink in quickly without leaving a greasy film. These not only soften your whiskers but also keep the skin beneath your beard healthy and hydrated.

Because beard oil is massaged from the roots to the ends, anything too thick can clog pores underneath, leading to irritation or those deep, painful beard pimples every guy dreads. Smart formulas use blends of light oils—often combined with extras like marula, sweet almond, squalane, or vitamin E—to boost moisture, strengthen hair, and calm inflamed skin without weighing things down. As long as the base oils are lightweight and absorbent, a multi-oil mix is exactly what you want.

Fragrance shouldn’t be the main reason you reach for a beard oil, especially if you have sensitive skin, but it can be a great bonus. Plenty of beard oils have masculine, cologne-quality scents that give the product some added value. Plus, it’ll give you something pleasant to smell on your mustache all day.

That being said, strong scents can easily trigger irritation, so stick to oils with a subtle aroma that comes naturally from the ingredients themselves. Added fragrances are common irritants, and even high concentrations of essential oils can cause redness or flare-ups.

If you’re not sure how your skin will react, do a quick patch test. Apply a small amount to one spot, then wait a few hours (or even overnight). No redness, itching, or bumps? You’re in the clear and good to use it everywhere.

I’ve had a beard for so long that I barely remember my face without one, which means I’ve spent the better part of two decades testing every type of beard product out there, including more oils than I can count. Over the past two years, I’ve compared notes with fellow Men’s Health editors, swapped favorites, and put a fresh batch of formulas through daily testing to see which ones actually deliver softer, healthier, better-looking whiskers.

With all that experience, I was able to narrow the field before spending months trying different oils on everything from short stubble to full-grown scruff. I looked at how well they hydrated, how fast they absorbed, how they felt on the skin underneath, and whether they left any greasy residue behind. Price, scent, and ingredient quality all factored in, too. What you’ll find below are my honest picks for the best beard oils worth buying in 2026, options that truly elevate your grooming routine, whether you’re rocking light stubble or a full-on mane.

For the best results, I like to treat my beard the same way I treat the hair on my head: regular washing and consistent conditioning. Clean it a few times a week with a beard-specific wash to remove buildup, then follow with a good beard oil. Before applying the oil, smooth out your beard with a comb, brush, or even your fingers so you’re starting with the shape you want.

Warm a small amount of oil between your palms and work in from the cheeks and chin, massaging it in the same way you’d apply a face moisturizer. Make sure you’re getting all the way down to the skin—that’s what keeps dryness, itch, and irritation away. If your beard is longer, finish by running your fingers through the length in downward strokes to coat every strand.

#4974. Sykeruns X7 electric dirt bike review: A lot of power for surprisingly little money

The mini electric dirt bike market has exploded over the last few years, with seemingly countless new brands offering everything from pint-sized electric pit bikes to surprisingly powerful off-road machines. The Sykeruns X7 falls somewhere in the middle, offering enough power to get into some serious trouble while keeping the price relatively approachable.

I’ve spent some time now riding the X7, and while it certainly isn’t the most refined electric dirt bike I’ve tested, there’s enough to like about what you’re getting for the money.

In fact, if you’re looking for a reasonably powerful electric dirt bike for recreational trail riding without spending several thousand dollars, this might be worth a closer look.

The Sykeruns X7 is a compact electric dirt bike featuring a 5,500W peak-rated motor, which translates to around 7.4 horsepower. That’s quite a bit of power for a bike at this price point of $1,699, especially considering that many similarly priced electric two-wheelers are significantly less powerful. Oh, and for our readers, we’ve gotten you set up with a 20% discount. Just use code ELECTREK20 to drop the price down to an impressive $1,359!

Sykeruns claims a top speed of 57 mph (92 km/h), though since this is an off-road only bike, you’ll rarely get the chance to put that claim to the test. I certainly didn’t, as I didn’t have a long enough and flat enough stretch of trail where I felt comfortable hitting nearly highway speeds on a low-cost e-moto.

The battery is a 60V 27Ah pack, providing 1,620 Wh of capacity. Sykeruns claims up to 60 miles (96 km) of range, though as with virtually every electric dirt bike, your actual range will depend heavily on how aggressively you’re riding. Fast trail riding, steep climbs, and repeated hard acceleration can eat through battery capacity much more quickly than leisurely cruising. Suffice it to say that you’ll likely not see the 60 mile figure in real world scenarios, but that’s still a fairly large battery.

The bike rolls on a 17-inch front wheel and 14-inch rear wheel, both wrapped in knobby off-road tires. Hydraulic disc brakes handle stopping duties, while an inverted suspension fork and rear monoshock help smooth out the bumps.

At 143 lb (65 kg), the X7 isn’t exactly featherweight, but it’s also far from being a full-size electric motorcycle.

The first thing I was surprised about with the X7 is that it offers a pretty decent amount of performance for the money. There’s enough power here to have some real fun, and the bike doesn’t feel like one of those underpowered mini electric motorcycles that struggles once you get beyond casual neighborhood speeds.

That said, I wouldn’t describe the acceleration as mind-blowing, either. We’re not talking about the kind of explosive power delivery you’d get from a high-end electric dirt bike costing several times as much. Instead, the X7 delivers a healthy amount of acceleration that feels appropriate for a recreational off-road machine.

And let’s be real here, that’s probably what most people shopping in this budget category are looking for.

The suspension is another area where the X7 earns a passing grade without necessarily winning any awards. The front fork and rear shock do their jobs, absorbing the bumps and ruts you’d expect to encounter on typical trails. It’s nothing I’d call plush, but I could see it doing light jumps with minimal air time.

Would I want to take this thing to a motocross track and start launching it off massive jumps? Not particularly. The suspension doesn’t have the premium feel or sophisticated damping of more expensive machines.

But for general trail riding, exploring dirt roads, and the occasional overlanding shenanigans, it’s perfectly serviceable. Not every electric dirt bike needs to be a competition-ready machine, and the X7 seems comfortable occupying that more recreational category.

I was also pleasantly surprised by the tires, which seem well suited to the bike’s intended purpose. The knobby tread offers a reasonable amount of grip for off-road riding, and I didn’t find myself immediately wishing for a tire upgrade.

The overall size is worth mentioning, too. This isn’t a particularly large electric dirt bike, but at my modest 5’7” (170 cm) height, I felt comfortable on it. The riding position didn’t feel overly cramped, and the bike was manageable enough that I didn’t feel like I was wrestling with an oversized machine.

Taller riders might find it a bit more compact than they’d prefer, but for average-height riders, the proportions seem reasonable.

If there’s one area where the X7 reminds you of its budget-friendly $1,699 price tag, it’s the overall level of refinement.

Nothing about the bike struck me as particularly premium. The components, finishes, and general construction are more in line with what I’d expect from a relatively inexpensive electric dirt bike.

But that’s not necessarily a criticism. There’s a difference between something feeling inexpensive and something feeling inadequate, and the X7 generally stays on the acceptable side of that line.

The controls are straightforward, the digital display provides the basic information you need, and the overall package feels focused on delivering usable performance rather than impressing riders with fancy features.

The grippy hydraulic brakes are also a welcome inclusion, especially considering the speeds this bike is capable of reaching. With a machine that can approach highway speeds, having proper motorcycle-style braking hardware is important.

Of course, long-term durability is a separate question. Budget electric dirt bikes don’t always have the same track record, parts availability, or established dealer networks as the more recognizable motorcycle brands. That’s something worth considering before purchasing, particularly if you plan to ride hard or frequently.

One thing I appreciate about the Sykeruns X7 is that the company makes its intended use fairly clear.

There’s a large red warning sticker on the bike explaining that it’s intended for off-road use only. That’s a good thing, especially in today’s market, where the lines between electric bicycles, electric dirt bikes, and electric motorcycles are becoming increasingly blurred, despite laws existing to keep these types of bikes out of the bike lane and off of public roads.

The X7 is absolutely not an electric bicycle. It doesn’t have pedals, it produces several thousand watts of power, and it’s capable of speeds far beyond anything permitted under electric bicycle regulations.

It’s an off-road electric motorcycle, plain and simple.

Interestingly, though, Sykeruns has equipped the bike with features like a tail light and turn signals, which could potentially give some riders the wrong impression.

Those are certainly useful features on a motorcycle, but they don’t magically make a vehicle street legal. Without the necessary certification, registration, and other road-use requirements, the X7 remains an off-road-only machine.

I worry that some buyers might see those lights and assume they can ride the bike around town like a small electric motorcycle. That’s not the case, and it’s important to understand that distinction before buying one.

After spending time with the Sykeruns X7, my biggest takeaway is that this is a reasonably capable electric dirt bike at a pretty compelling price.

It’s not the best electric dirt bike I’ve ever ridden. The suspension is fairly basic, the build quality is unremarkable, and there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about the design.

But for $1,699 (or $1,359 if you use the code ELECTREK20 to take 20% off!), you’re getting a 5.5 kW peak-rated electric motorcycle with a sizable battery, proper off-road tires, hydraulic brakes, and enough performance to have some genuine fun on the trails.

I wouldn’t say that the X7 here is trying to compete with more up-market electric dirt bikes from the likes of Juiced, Sur-Ron or Talaria on overall refinement, but they make this type of riding much more accessible.

And that’s really where I think the X7 makes the most sense.

If you’re an experienced dirt bike rider looking for a highly refined machine with excellent suspension and premium components, you’ll probably want to keep shopping.

But if you’re someone who wants a fun electric dirt bike for exploring private property, cruising around trails where motorized riding is permitted, or just enjoying some recreational off-road riding without spending a fortune, the Sykeruns X7 offers a pretty reasonable package.

It doesn’t need to be amazing at everything. At this price, being pretty good at most things is already an accomplishment.
